note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for treatment planning following diagnosis of high-grade prostate cancer.

Recently retired warehouse worker with a known diagnosis of prostate cancer. The patient has a history of type 2 diabetes and hypercholesterolaemia, managed with metformin, atorvastatin, and simvastatin. He also suffers from osteoarthritis. He is married and lives in a multi-generational household with his adult son, who acts as his caregiver and holds lasting power of attorney. He cycles approximately 20 km twice weekly and consumes 4 units of alcohol per week. His IPSS score is 14, indicating moderate lower urinary tract symptoms. He reports no bone pain or haematuria. He has a visual impairment and requires large-print correspondence. Recent quarterly review with the diabetes nurse was unremarkable.

On digital rectal examination, the prostate feels normal in size and consistency with no palpable nodules, correlating with a clinical stage of cT1c. General examination is unremarkable with stable vital signs and no signs of metastatic disease.

next_of_kin: Adult son (acts as caregiver, lasting power of attorney)
